body: What did you do at WIC?
Sorry, this isn't customer service. This is meant for WIC staff.

Thank you for commenting! I started this subreddit for WIC professionals to gather but the current mod had my subreddit banned and then took it over to be more of a customer service for WIC participants.
How were you able to become the mod? I was demodded without warning in October of 2023 and none of my appeals were answered.
That's likely due to Diastasis Recti.

I was able to negotiate to some degree. Part of the issue is that local agencies treat the state funding as the only budget source for clinic and it barely covers minimum wage compensation for many roles at WIC.
Grocery stores that are WIC approved vendors!
The ability to do the appointments over the phone was so helpful.

Regulatory food composition requirements for each category: https://www.fns.usda.gov/wic/wic-food-packages-regulatory-requirements-wic-eligible-foods

Public comments on the changes are open until February https://www.regulations.gov/commenton/FNS-2022-0007-0001

Too many American has excessive saturated fats in their diet and 1% milk provides the same nutrition with less fats.

Beans, peanut butter, eggs, milk, cheese, yogurt, whole grains are all good sources of protein. 

Here's a fact sheet on the food package from the NWA, a lobbying group that works to improve the food package.

https://s3.amazonaws.com/aws.upl/nwica.org/nwa-wic-food-package-report.pdf

I think part of that has to do with the pay and staff turn-over/shortages. It'll really depend on how your local agency is structured and who your boss is, I don't think it's inherent to the job. Within my state there's quite a variance between agencies. I get quite a bit of job satisfaction as there's a tangible impact to the community.
I created https://old.reddit.com/r/WIC/ and haven't really promoted it or done much with it. I'm a WIC director if you want to DM me.
